case_title: Ansar Ahmad v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr.
previous_criminal_record: Yes. Both respondents have a chequered criminal record; earlier both were found guilty under s.302 IPC.
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated as a personal relationship. Alleged motive: the victim's father-in-law was a witness in an earlier criminal case against one respondent (prior enmity).
statutory_provisions: IPC s.147, s.148, s.149, s.307, s.302, s.120-B, s.34; Explosive Substances Act s.3, s.4
evidence_type: Eyewitness; recovery (two country-made pistols, magazines, mobile phone, cash); disclosure statement of an arrested accused; motive material
confession: None. A disclosure by another arrested accused implicated one respondent; the Court did not rely on it as a confession or finding against the respondents.
aggravating_circumstances: Murder in broad daylight; alleged contract killing; material indicating motive; both respondents have criminal records; alleged involvement in the present case while on bail in an earlier case
trial_court_outcome: Not stated. Trial was ongoing with only one witness examined when the Supreme Court decided the appeal.
high_court_outcome: Bail applications allowed on 23.09.2021; both respondents granted regular bail
neutral_facts: The victim, the son of the complainant, was present with the complainant and companions outside a bank branch when one accused allegedly threw a grenade at him. Other accused then allegedly began indiscriminate firing. The victim died on the spot and another person present was injured. Two persons were caught at the scene with the help of the public. One gave his name and the other did not. Two country-made pistols, two magazines and a mobile phone were recovered from them. A sum of cash was also recovered from the persons apprehended, as stated in the complainant's first information report. During interrogation, one arrested person allegedly disclosed that another person and his brother had sent the arrested persons to commit the killing. The case was described as a contract killing. The investigation found that one alleged accused was present at the spot during the occurrence, while the other was alleged to be part of the conspiracy to eliminate the victim. The alleged motive was that the victim's father-in-law had been a witness in an earlier criminal case registered against that alleged conspirator. Eyewitnesses included the complainant and two others.
physical_harm: Death of the victim (Ashfaque Ahmad); injuries to Razi Ahmad @ Manu
premeditation_planning: Court observed prima facie that it was apparently a contract killing with a conspiracy to eliminate the victim; not finally determined
motive: alleged: the victim's father-in-law was a witness in a criminal case against one respondent, who had been convicted under s.302 IPC in that case
key_evidence_accepted: Prima facie only: eyewitness account of the complainant and two others; two accused arrested at the spot; material indicating motive
witness_credibility: Not assessed. The Court expressly declined to express views on the merits; one eyewitness had yet to depose.
post_offence_conduct: Not stated for the offence. During trial, respondents sought exemption from personal appearance and one was absent with non-bailable warrants issued.
bail_history: Bail granted to both respondents by the High Court on 23.09.2021 (set aside by Supreme Court). One respondent was on bail in an earlier s.302 IPC case when the present offence allegedly occurred; co-accused Satish Kumar @ Satai's bail was rejected by the High Court on 03.09.2021.
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 23.09.2021; Supreme Court: 18.04.2023
legal_representation: For appellant (complainant): Siddharth Dave, Sr. Adv. For respondents (accused): Basant R, Sr. Adv., and others. For State: Sharan Thakur, A.A.G. and Additional Advocate General.
investigation_status: FIR registered (Case Crime No. 17 of 2018); investigation found respondents' alleged involvement; trial pending with only one witness examined
procedural_irregularity: High Court did not consider relevant material while granting bail; reasons for distinguishing the co-accused's rejected bail were not found convincing
appeal_history: Trial court: not stated. High Court: bail granted 23.09.2021. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, bail orders set aside, respondents directed to surrender.
prosecution_argument: Challenge to grant of bail; detailed prosecution submissions are not recorded in the judgment
defence_argument: Counsel submitted that cogent circumstances are needed to cancel bail and there were no supervening circumstances warranting cancellation
legal_principle_applied: Bail must reflect judicial application of mind to parameters (gravity, criminal antecedents, influence on witnesses, tampering, misuse of bail). Distinction between challenge to grant of bail and cancellation for supervening circumstances; need to ensure vital witnesses are examined before bail
precedent_relied_upon: Ash Mohammad v. Shivraj Singh @ Lalla Babu (2012) 9 SCC 446; Puran v. Rambilas (2001) 6 SCC 338; Venkatesan Balsubramaniyan v. Intelligence Officer, DRI Bangalore (2020) 13 SCALE 191
judicial_aggravating_factors: Contract killing in broad daylight; material indicating motive; criminal records including prior s.302 IPC conviction; alleged offence committed while on bail; trial stalled by non-appearance; eyewitness yet to depose
other_sentence_order: Respondents to surrender before Trial Court forthwith, with liberty to seek bail after examination of all eye witnesses; Trial Court directed to decide case expeditiously and endeavour to conclude trial within one year
